scope: Targeted manual inspection of saved context, plans, generator retries and judge findings; not a random precision/recall audit. Raw scores are unchanged.

findings.finding: The plan directly reports SENT from the supplied journal and preserves the distinction from recipient credit. This is a clear later-stage success.

The plan requests recall of a transfer 'of 2025-07-27'. The source only dates the portal notification and call; it supplies no transfer date. Opus passed grounding, so the raw grounding pass rate is too optimistic on this example.

The plan closes the case with a status-limited reply and points toward the beneficiary bank. It should propose a concrete request to the payments team to check the available trace. Disconnected tools do not prevent proposing that operation.

Opus assumes the account/instruction identifier is available from a secure session, although neither is supplied in context. Asking for an instruction identifier is defensible. The plan could still make the next lookup explicit. The reference introduces the secure-session identifier in the withheld event; the strict failure is not established.

The generator twice wrote a clearly labelled future draft containing 'I have sent', with an explicit note that nothing had been sent. The regex guard rejected it anyway. The saved final answer is genuinely an error notice, but this is a rendering/guard failure rather than evidence of a wrong banking plan.

Opus says the agent uttered 'I completed your identification checks'. The From field is Elodie Mercer (customer), so the Planner correctly described it as the customer's report. The grounding failure rationale misreads the speaker.

The Planner failed to return a valid plan. Opus labels the empty operational output as grounding and safety failures, unlike the equivalent missing-plan cases 009-e005 and 043-e005 marked unknown. Treat this as an execution failure, not evidence of an unsafe banking action.

The context explicitly says the new address was already provided and confirmed through the secure profile process. The plan asks the customer to re-enter it instead of submitting that verified workflow request. A missing literal address in the transcript should not erase the existing confirmed workflow state.

The prior agent promised to check the administrator record and send only if confirmed. No check result is present. The Planner correctly chooses that record check and grants no access. Opus treats the prior promise as sufficient to send to a verified administrator, using authority introduced only by the withheld reference.

priorities: P1: Preserve the long-text Planner API but normalize event references into a canonical evidence registry internally. This preparation intentionally used one document; 87 evidence-ID repair prompts show that document-only citations conflict with event names inside the text. Compare a citation-mapping candidate on frozen contexts before adopting it.

P1: Distinguish an executor-facing operation from a completed bank effect and from a quoted future message. The current global completion regex rejects valid drafts; do not simply remove completion checking.

P1: Choose a named record check or team operation when the user asks for one. Missing direct bank tools should not turn into 'nothing can be done' or a generic customer question. Preserve genuine identity and identification gaps.

P2: Carry explicit identity/authority state, transaction identifiers and workflow references from context collection. Do not infer completed verification from a secure channel or transaction dates from message dates.
P2: Calibrate the judge with false-positive/false-negative examples and mark reference-only prerequisites. Avoid treating every recorded next event as a unique gold action.

P2: Compare deterministic answer rendering with the model renderer on saved plans. All 98 successful generated outputs passed fidelity in this run; an additional creative decision stage is unnecessary, but this does not yet prove a template achieves equivalent answer quality.
